source_title: 2027 Maserati GranTurismo, GranCabrio launched; priced from Rs 2.62 crore - Autocar India
source_excerpt:
Maserati India has launched the 2027 GranTurismo and GranCabrio , with prices starting at Rs 2.62 crore and Rs 2.91 crore, respectively. Updates include a refreshed exterior and interior, along with mechanical upgrades. Delivery timelines are yet to be confirmed.
Trofeo versions produce more power – 590hp
Folgore versions’ claimed WLTP range rises to 540km
New ‘Country’ drive mode raises ride height by 20mm
More exterior and interior personalisation options via Fuoriserie programme

The GranTurismo is priced from Rs 2.62 crore to Rs 3.14 crore, while the GranCabrio costs Rs 2.91 crore to Rs 3.30 crore.
2027 Maserati GranTurismo, GranCabrio powertrains
The 2027 GranTurismo and GranCabrio are offered in combustion-powered (490 and Trofeo) and all-electric (Folgore) versions, with the 490 replacing the pre-facelift model’s entry-spec Modena variant. The ICE versions retain the 3.0-litre twin-turbo petrol ‘Nettuno’ V6 engine, which produces 490hp and 600Nm in the 490 guise and 590hp and 650Nm in the Trofeo variant. The Trofeo variant’s power has increased by 50hp compared with the pre-facelift model. Both ICE versions get an 8-speed gearbox that sends power to all four wheels but has been recalibrated for quicker responses.
The base GranTurismo has a claimed 0-100kph time of 3.9 seconds and a top speed of 302kph; the more powerful Trofeo variant drops that to 3.5 seconds and can reach 320kph. Meanwhile, the GranCabrio has a 0-100kph time of 4 seconds in the 490 guise and 3.6 seconds in the Trofeo guise, with top speeds of 300kph and 316kph, respectively.
The electric versions of the 2027 GranTurismo and GranCabrio retain the 92.5kWh battery pack paired with three e-motors – one at the front and two at the rear. Maximum output stands at 761hp and 1,340Nm, enabling a 0-100kph time of 2.5 seconds for the GranTurismo Folgore and 2.8 seconds for the GranCabrio Folgore. Their claimed top speeds stand at 325kph and 290kph, respectively.
Global-spec Maserati GranTurismo Folgore (left), GranCabrio Folgore (right)
All models come with an air suspension setup as standard. Only the base-spec and Folgore variants get a new ‘Country’ mode, which replaces the comfort mode from the pre-facelift version and increases ground clearance by 20mm at up to 120kph. Maserati says this driving mode makes the car more capable on uneven road surfaces. Meanwhile, the ‘Corsa’ track mode is exclusive to the Trofeo.
Thanks to a new system that disconnects the front motor when all-wheel traction is not required, the claimed WLTP range has increased from 450km to 540km. Using a 270kW DC fast charger, the battery can be topped up from 20 to 80 percent in a claimed 18 minutes. AC charging support is rated at 22kW, and 100km of range can be added in an hour.
2027 Maserati GranTurismo, GranCabrio exterior
Visually, changes to the exterior of the 2027 GranTurismo and GranCabrio are mainly focused on the fascia. The front bumper takes inspiration from the MCPura, with an aggressive look, reshaped air intakes for better downforce and a redesigned splitter. Meanwhile, the LED tail-lamps have clear-lens detailing. The GranCabrio’s roof opens and closes in 14 seconds and 16 seconds, respectively. All-electric Folgore versions get an exclusive design for the front and rear bumpers, aero-optimised alloy wheels, illuminated fender vents and badges finished in copper.
Additionally, Maserati has introduced new paint options for the exterior, badges and exhaust tips via its Fuoriserie personalisation programme. New paint choices include Green Jupiter Matte, Blu Denim, Bronzo Lucido, Bronzo Matte, Grigio Mistero, Rosso Velluto and Oro Lirico. There’s also the option of ‘Tridente’ rims, which get a gloss-black design inspired by the MCPura and 10mm more track width.
2027 Maserati GranTurismo, GranCabrio interior
Inside, the GranTurismo and GranCabrio get a new race-inspired octagonal steering wheel with dark satin aluminium spokes, a redesigned digital clock with an octagonal metal rim featuring new graphics, metal knobs for the drive selector, and a parking function integrated into the steering-wheel paddles. Maserati has also added a new system to track driver behaviour and fatigue. Lastly, like the exterior, the interior can be specced with a variety of customisation options.
